beats.text: Zombies won't kill you first. Dirty water will. Here's how I stayed alive.
I'm Cole. I used to teach science. Now I teach survival.
I picked this library on purpose. Stone walls, one door, and windows too high to climb.
But on day three, the taps stopped running.
Here's the science. You can last about three weeks without food. But only about three days without water.
So I went to the river. But river water can carry bacteria and parasites.
They make you sick, and you lose even more water. Out here, that can kill you.
Step one. Pour it through a cloth to catch the dirt.
beats.title: FILTER THROUGH CLOTH
beats.sub: Clears dirt. Does NOT kill germs.

beats.text: Step two. Bring it to a rolling boil for one full minute. Three minutes if you're high in the mountains.
beats.title: ROLLING BOIL: 1 MINUTE

beats.text: Step three. Let it cool, and store it in clean, covered jars.
beats.title: STORE IT COVERED

beats.text: But there's a problem. The smoke from my fire can be seen for miles.
So, would you rather keep boiling water and risk the smoke? Or put out the fire and live on what you have left?
beats.opt1: Keep boiling water and risk the smoke
beats.opt2: Put out the fire and live on what you have left
